newsitem.title: USA: Ford adds $500 to '96 Taurus incentives.
newsitem.headline: Ford adds $500 to '96 Taurus incentives.

text.p: Ford Motor Co., in a bid to clear out remaining inventories of 1996 Taurus sedans, said Thursday it added $500 to existing incentives, bring the car's total rebate to $1,500 only a year after its introduction.
The increased incentives on the Taurus come two weeks after the car lost its lead as the best selling car in the United States when August sales were reported.
For the first eight months of the year, Ford sold 250,212 Tauruses, 1,409 units fewer than the Honda Accord.
The Taurus faces tough competition from both a redesigned Toyota Camry and a slew of new mid-size sedans from General Motors Corp.
Ford spokeswoman Joy Wolfe said the higher incentives became effective this week and do not apply to 1997 Taurus models and expire Oct. 1.
On Monday, Ford Chairman Alex Trotman was asked whether Taurus will remain the best selling car in the United States. "Time will tell," he said.
